newsitem.title: ITALY: PDS rejects Italian Renewal Euro-tax amendment.
newsitem.headline: PDS rejects Italian Renewal Euro-tax amendment.

text.p: The leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), Massimo D'Alema, said on Thursday that a proposal by coalition partner Italian Renewal to amend the government's Euro-tax plan was unacceptable, PDS sources said.

They said D'Alema, whose party is the biggest in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government, told a party meeting that an amendment to the plan submitted by Italian Renewal in the Senate (upper house) altered the balance of the plan in an unacceptable manner.
D'Alema made his remarks ahead of a meeting of the coalition's parliamentary party leaders in the Senate that has been called for 1730 GMT to discuss differences over the plan for the 1997 Euro-tax.
It aims to raise a total of 12.5 trillion lire towards an overall 1997 budget of 62.5 trillion lire meant to help Italy meet the terms for membership of Europe's planned single currency.
Prodi's "Olive Tree" coalition parties agree on the amount to be raised but are at odds over how the burden of the Euro-tax levy should be imposed on different categories of taxpayers.
